views.name: paper_base
views.body_sql: SELECT paperId, title, venueId, year, numCiting, numCitedBy, journalId FROM paper

params.description: Base normalized view of papers: one row per paper with identifying info and precomputed citation counts.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic paper attributes (id, title, venue, year, journal) for display or filtering | Filter or group by paper-level fields when composing downstream aggregations (e.g., counts by year or venue) | Use as a stable grain when joining to one-row-per-paper dimensions or when building further aggregated metrics (e.g., average citations per paper) | Serve as the FROM-source for joins that enrich paper rows with authors, datasets, keyphrases, or venue/journal details (provided joins are cardinality-safe as described below)
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived directly from base column paper.paperId | title: paper title — derived directly from base column paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper was presented/published — derived directly from base column paper.venueId | year: publication year of the paper — derived directly from base column paper.year | numCiting: number of outgoing citation edges from this paper (papers this paper cites) — derived directly from base column paper.numCiting | numCitedBy: number of incoming citation edges to this paper (papers citing this paper) — derived directly from base column paper.numCitedBy | journalId: identifier of the journal (if applicable) for the paper — derived directly from base column paper.journalId
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy | paper.journalId
params.metric: numCiting = <base metric column paper.numCiting>  -- already stored per paper (no aggregation in this view) | numCitedBy = <base metric column paper.numCitedBy>  -- already stored per paper (no aggregation in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId or on venueId/journalId — safe when joining on venueId or journalId to bring venue/journal descriptive attributes if those views are one-row-per-venue or one-row-per-journal respectively, because paper_base is one-row-per-paper and venue/journal rows do not duplicate paper rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to papers_per_venue_agg or paper_citation_counts_agg on paperId only if those aggregates are computed at paper grain (they are labelled as AGG so confirm their grain). If those sibling aggregates are at paper grain, joining on paperId is safe because it's 1:1. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_paper_counts_ranked or papers_per_author_agg only after aggregating or restricting to one row per paper (e.g., join to a pre-aggregated table that is one-row-per-paper-author or use an EXISTS/subquery). Do NOT directly inner-join to papers_per_author_agg or author_paper_counts_ranked if they are one-to-many (author -> many papers or paper -> many authors) because that would multiply paper_base rows and thus duplicate the per-paper metrics (numCiting, numCitedBy). | do NOT join directly to paper_authors, paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, or citation_edges without re-aggregation: these sibling views represent one-to-many relationships (paper -> authors, paper -> datasets, paper -> keyphrases, and citation edges). Direct joins will duplicate paper_base rows and therefore overcount measures unless you first aggregate the many-side (for example, aggregate authors into an array or counts per paper) or perform joins in a way that preserves paper grain (e.g., lateral subqueries that return single summarized row per paper). | When composing metrics (e.g., average numCitedBy per venue), perform aggregation after joining: SELECT venueId, AVG(numCitedBy) FROM paper_base GROUP BY venueId — avoid joining in any one-to-many enrichments before this aggregation unless those enrichments are themselves reduced to one row per paper. | If you need author-level metrics combined with per-paper metrics, first aggregate or rank authors per paper to one row (for example, primary author) and then join that 1:1 result to paper_base to avoid duplicating numCiting/numCitedBy.

views.description: Canonical normalized projection of the paper table exposing core attributes and measures. Use this as the single-row-per-paper foundation for joins, aggregates, and ranking (keeps original column names and provides a deterministic null-safe projection). | Use for: List or filter papers by attributes (title, year, venue, journal); Base relation to join authors, keyphrases, datasets, citations; Compute paper-level measures or trends over time

views.name: paper_with_venue_journal
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.paperId, p.title, p.venueId, v.venueName, p.journalId, j.journalName, p.year, p.numCiting, p.numCitedBy
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN venue v ON p.venueId = v.venueId
LEFT JOIN journal j ON p.journalId = j.journalId

params.description: One-row-per-paper view combining paper attributes with their venue and journal names and basic citation counts.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve paper-level metadata (title, year) together with identifying venue and journal names. | Report or filter papers by venue or journal while preserving per-paper citation counts. | Start point for composing aggregates at the paper grain (e.g., sum or average citation counts across a set of papers). | Joinable input for author, dataset, keyphrase, or other dimensions when you need paper-level detail enriched with venue/journal labels.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — from paper.paperId | title: paper title string — from paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue associated with the paper — from paper.venueId | venueName: human-readable name of the venue — from venue.venueName (via LEFT JOIN on venueId) | journalId: identifier of the journal associated with the paper — from paper.journalId | journalName: human-readable name of the journal — from journal.journalName (via LEFT JOIN on journalId) | year: publication year of the paper — from paper.year | numCiting: number of outgoing citations made by this paper (paper.numCiting) — base numeric column preserved as-is | numCitedBy: number of incoming citations to this paper (paper.numCitedBy) — base numeric column preserved as-is
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | venue.venueName | paper.journalId | journal.journalName | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy
params.metric: numCiting = paper.numCiting (base integer/count stored on paper; not an aggregate in this view) | numCitedBy = paper.numCitedBy (base integer/count stored on paper; not an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author- or author-aggregated views on paperId (for example paper_authors JOIN paper_with_venue_journal ON paper_with_venue_journal.paperId = paper_authors.paperId) — safe only if the target side is guaranteed to be one-row-per-paper (e.g., an authorship summary aggregated to paperId); otherwise re-aggregate after the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base on paperId — safe because paper_base is the normalized base at paper grain and will be one-row-per-paper, so measures numCiting and numCitedBy are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_citation_counts_agg on paperId — safe if that view is one-row-per-paper (an aggregate keyed by paperId). | do NOT directly join to one-to-many child tables/views such as paper_authors (raw authorship rows), paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, or citation_edges without careful aggregation, because those are many-rows-per-paper and will duplicate this view's measures (numCiting, numCitedBy) when joined. Instead, either: | - aggregate the child table to one-row-per-paper first (e.g., COUNT(*) or ARRAY_AGG grouped by paperId) and then join, or | - perform the join and then re-aggregate back to paper grain (GROUP BY paperId) ensuring measures are recomputed correctly. | joining to venue or journal dimension tables is safe on venueId or journalId respectively because the view already LEFT JOINs to those dimensions; additional joins to other one-row-per-venue or one-row-per-journal aggregates (e.g., papers_per_venue_agg) should be on venueId or journalId and are safe only if those targets are one-row-per-venue/journal and you intend to associate venue-level metrics to each paper (these will not duplicate per-paper measures). | when composing metrics across this view (for example summing numCitedBy across a set of papers), treat numCitedBy and numCiting as base numeric columns and apply your aggregate on them after any joins that preserve paper-level uniqueness. | reasoning: this view's declared grain is one row per paperId (from paper). Any join that preserves that 1:1 relationship per paperId will not duplicate the numeric measures. Any join that introduces N>1 rows per paperId must be aggregated back to paperId to avoid multiplying counts.

views.description: Denormalized paper rows with their venue and journal names. Useful for reporting or filtering papers by venueName or journalName without repeating join logic. One row per paper. | Use for: Show papers along with venue and journal names; Filter papers by venueName or journalName; Aggregate measures (numCiting/numCitedBy) by venue or journal
validated_on: Retrieve a list of distinct papers, including the paper ID, title, year of publication, and citation category, that have been co-authored by "Peter Mertens" and "Dina Barbian" and published after the year 2015.

views.name: paper_authors
views.body_sql:
SELECT w.paperId, w.authorId, a.authorName
FROM writes w
JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: Provides the relationship between papers and their authors (one row per paperId + authorId) including the author's name.
params.when_to_use: List all authors for a given paper (or set of papers). | List all papers for a given author (or set of authors). | Compose author-level attributes (e.g., authorName) onto paper-level datasets or aggregates without changing paper-author multiplicity. | Build further aggregations by counting distinct paperId or authorId across the paper-author pairs.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper; derived from writes.paperId (base table column writes.paperId) | authorId: identifier of the author; derived from writes.authorId (base table column writes.authorId) | authorName: display name of the author; derived from author.authorName (base table column author.authorName)
params.metric: This view has no aggregated metrics. All output columns are direct projections from base columns: paperId = writes.paperId, authorId = writes.authorId, authorName = author.authorName.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base on paperId — safe because paper_base is one-row-per-paper (joining this view to that will produce one row per paper-author pair as intended, and will not duplicate any measures maintained at the paper-author grain). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_paper_counts_ranked on authorId — safe when the target view is one-row-per-author (author-level aggregates). Joining a one-row-per-author relation to this view will attach author-level attributes to each paper-author row without duplicating measures at the paper-author grain. | DO NOT join this view to one-to-many siblings (e.g., paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges) directly if you intend to preserve counts or aggregates from this view: those joins are many-to-many relative to the paper-author grain and will duplicate rows/measures. Instead, either (a) aggregate the target one-to-many view to the same grain first (for example aggregate paper_keyphrases to unique paperId before joining), or (b) re-aggregate after the join using DISTINCT counts or GROUP BY the intended grain (paperId, authorId) to avoid multiplication. | When composing with paper_with_venue_journal (one-row-per-paper expected), join on paperId — safe because it is one-row-per-paper and will not duplicate this view's rows beyond the intended paper-author multiplicity. | When composing with papers_per_author_agg or paper_citation_counts_agg (aggregates at paper- or author-level), ensure you understand their grain: aggregate-level joins to this view are safe if the aggregate is one-row-per-author or one-row-per-paper respectively; otherwise re-aggregate to match the paper-author grain before joining. | To compute measures such as 'number of authors per paper' from this view, aggregate COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId on this view itself rather than joining to writes/author and risking duplication. | Summary rule: this view's grain is (paperId, authorId). Any join that preserves or collapses to that grain (one-to-one or many-to-one into either paperId or authorId) is safe. Any join that introduces additional multiplicity at the paper or author level (many-to-many) must be pre-aggregated or followed by re-aggregation to avoid multiplying rows/measures.

views.description: Exploded relation of paper-author pairs with author names (one row per authorship). Use for author-level aggregations, co-author network construction, or counting authors per paper. | Use for: List authors for a paper; Count papers per author or authors per paper; Build co-authorship edges (join on paperId)

views.name: paper_datasets
views.body_sql:
SELECT pd.paperId, pd.datasetId, d.datasetName
FROM paperDataset pd
JOIN dataset d ON pd.datasetId = d.datasetId

params.description: Maps papers to the datasets they reference, returning one row per (paperId, datasetId) with the dataset name.
params.when_to_use: List the datasets used by a specific paper or set of papers (e.g., which datasets does paper X reference?). | Count or aggregate papers per dataset when starting from the paper-dataset pairs. | Join dataset metadata (datasetName) onto paper-level queries that already operate at the paper-dataset grain. | Filter papers by dataset attributes by composing this view with dataset-level filters or aggregations.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from paperDataset.paperId (pd.paperId). | datasetId: identifier of the dataset — derived from paperDataset.datasetId (pd.datasetId). | datasetName: human-readable name of the dataset — derived from dataset.datasetName (d.datasetName).
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view: all outputs are base columns projected from joins (no aggregates or computed measures).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (NORM) on paperId — safe because paper_base is one row per paper (or normalized paper identifier), so joining paper_datasets (one row per paperId,datasetId) to paper_base on paperId will not duplicate rows for additional measures that are defined at the paper-dataset grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dataset (base table) on datasetId — safe because dataset is one row per datasetId; joining brings additional dataset attributes without duplicating paper-dataset rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many views/tables that expand per paper (e.g., paper_authors or paper_keyphrases) on paperId without re-aggregation, because those joins can multiply rows: for example, joining paper_datasets to paper_authors (which is many authors per paper) will create multiple rows per (paperId,datasetId) — to preserve correct counts/metrics, first aggregate the many-side (e.g., author counts per paper) or join via a deduplicated key. | do NOT join to aggregation views that are at paper grain (e.g., paper_citation_counts_agg) expecting to retain one-row-per-dataset measure without checking grain compatibility. If the target aggregated view is at paper grain (one row per paper), joining it to paper_datasets will replicate the paper-level measure across each dataset used by that paper — this is valid if you intend per (paper,dataset) replication, but unsafe if you want dataset-level metrics. In that case, either re-aggregate after the join or aggregate paper_datasets up to datasetId before joining. | If composing dataset-level metrics (e.g., papers per dataset), aggregate paper_datasets grouped by datasetId first (COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or COUNT(*) depending on deduplication needs) and then join to dataset for names — this avoids duplication from downstream joins. | When joining with sibling JOIN views that are one-row-per-(paperId, otherId) (e.g., other paper-associated entities), ensure you either (a) join on both keys when available to maintain one-row-per-(paperId,otherId, datasetId) semantics, or (b) pre-aggregate the many-side to the desired grain before joining to avoid unintended multiplicative effects.

views.description: Exploded relation of paper-dataset pairs with dataset names (one row per paper-dataset association). Use to find papers using a dataset or to aggregate dataset usage. | Use for: List datasets used by a paper; Count papers using each dataset; Filter papers by datasetName

views.name: paper_keyphrases
views.body_sql:
SELECT pk.paperId, pk.keyphraseId, k.keyphraseName
FROM paperKeyphrase pk
JOIN keyphrase k ON pk.keyphraseId = k.keyphraseId

params.description: Maps papers to their keyphrases, returning one row per (paperId, keyphraseId) with the keyphrase name.
params.when_to_use: List all keyphrases associated with a specific paper (e.g., given paperId). | Find all papers that include a specific keyphrase (e.g., given keyphraseId or keyphraseName). | Filter or join papers by their keyphrases when composing larger queries (e.g., to restrict a paper set to those containing certain keyphrases). | Build aggregations on top of paper–keyphrase pairs (e.g., count keyphrases per paper, count papers per keyphrase) by re-aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from paperKeyphrase.paperId (base table column pk.paperId). | keyphraseId: identifier of the keyphrase — derived from paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId (base table column pk.keyphraseId). | keyphraseName: human-readable keyphrase text — derived from keyphrase.keyphraseName (base table column k.keyphraseName).
params.metric: This view is at the grain (paperId, keyphraseId) and does not define pre-aggregated numeric measures. Derived measures should be defined by aggregating rows from this view. Examples: | paper_keyphrase_count_per_paper = COUNT(keyphraseId) GROUP BY paperId | paper_count_per_keyphrase = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) GROUP BY keyphraseId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (or other one-row-per-paper views such as paper_with_venue_journal) on paperId — safe because this view has at most one row per (paperId, keyphraseId) and joining to a one-row-per-paper dimension will not duplicate aggregated measures if you aggregate after the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to keyphrase (or any one-row-per-keyphrase dimension) on keyphraseId — safe for the same reason: keyphrase is one-row-per-keyphrase, so it does not multiply this view's rows. | UNSAFE to directly join to one-to-many children of paper (for example paper_authors, paper_datasets, citation_edges) without re-aggregation: joining this view to a one-to-many relationship on paperId (or keyphraseId) will multiply rows and thus duplicate counts/metrics unless you re-aggregate. For example, joining paper_keyphrases to paper_authors on paperId will produce rows for every (paperId, keyphraseId, author) combination — you must either (a) aggregate measures from paper_keyphrases first (e.g., count keyphrases per paper) and then join to authors, or (b) join then re-aggregate to the intended grain. | When composing metrics across siblings that are aggregated (papers_per_author_agg, paper_citation_counts_agg, papers_per_venue_agg): do NOT inner-join this view directly to those pre-aggregated result sets unless the join keys are aligned and you understand the grains. Instead, aggregate this view to the same grain as the sibling view before joining (e.g., produce paper-level keyphrase counts before joining to paper-level aggregates). | Safe pattern examples: | - To get number of keyphrases per paper and then join to paper_citation_counts_agg: first compute keyphrase_count_per_paper = SELECT paperId, COUNT(keyphraseId) AS keyphrase_count FROM paper_keyphrases GROUP BY paperId; then join keyphrase_count_per_paper to paper_citation_counts_agg ON paperId. | - To list papers for a given keyphraseName: filter this view by keyphraseName and join to paper_base ON paperId to fetch paper metadata — no duplication because paper_base is one-row-per-paper. | Summary rule: treat paper_keyphrases as a detailed, one-row-per-(paperId,keyphraseId) relationship table. When joining to dimensions at the paper or keyphrase grain, it is safe. When joining to other one-to-many tables, either aggregate first or accept and handle the multiplicative effect by re-aggregating to the desired grain.

views.description: Exploded relation of paper-keyphrase pairs with keyphrase names (one row per paper-keyphrase association). Useful for textual/topic analysis, counting papers per keyphrase, or filtering by keyphraseName. | Use for: Find keyphrases for a paper; Count papers per keyphrase; Filter papers by keyphraseName
validated_on: Could you please find the distinct IDs of papers that were authored by both John Doe and Jane Smith, and have been cited more than 5 times? This information is really important to me!

views.name: citation_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.citingPaperId, cp.title AS citingTitle, c.citedPaperId, cpp.title AS citedTitle
FROM cite c
LEFT JOIN paper cp ON c.citingPaperId = cp.paperId
LEFT JOIN paper cpp ON c.citedPaperId = cpp.paperId

params.description: Provides one row per citation edge connecting a citing paper to a cited paper, with both papers' titles.
params.when_to_use: List all citation relationships between papers (who cites whom). | Compose with paper-level data when you need titles or identifiers for both ends of a citation edge. | Build graph analytics or edge-level aggregations (degree, edge filtering) before aggregating to papers or authors. | Filter or join citation edges by paper attributes (venue, authors, keyphrases) by joining on the appropriate paper ID column.
params.output_schema: citingPaperId: identifier of the citing paper; derived from cite.citingPaperId (base table cite). | citingTitle: title of the citing paper; derived from paper.title joined as cp.title where cp.paperId = cite.citingPaperId. | citedPaperId: identifier of the cited paper; derived from cite.citedPaperId (base table cite). | citedTitle: title of the cited paper; derived from paper.title joined as cpp.title where cpp.paperId = cite.citedPaperId.
params.metric: There are no aggregate metrics in this view; all output columns are base columns or direct lookups. (No derived aggregate expressions.)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (or other paper-level JOIN views such as paper_with_venue_journal, paper_authors (if used only for author-level single-row lookup per paper), paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases) on citingPaperId = paper.paperId — safe when the target view is one-row-per-paper because citation edges are one-row-per-(citingPaperId,citedPaperId) and will not be duplicated by a one-row-per-paper lookup. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (or other one-row-per-paper views) on citedPaperId = paper.paperId — safe for the same reason as above. | do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many view (for example: paper_authors, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, or any author- or dataset-level view that produces multiple rows per paper) without first aggregating that one-to-many side to one row per paper (or re-aggregating after the join). Joining directly to a one-to-many table will duplicate citation-edge rows and thus multiply counts or other edge-level measures. | When composing aggregations over citation_edges (for example, count of outgoing citations per paper), perform the aggregation at the citation_edges level (GROUP BY citingPaperId) or, if joining additional one-to-many dimensions, aggregate the additional dimension to one row per paper before joining to preserve correct cardinality. | If you need author- or venue-level measures combined with citation edges, either (a) aggregate citation_edges up to paper and then join to author/venue aggregates, or (b) reduce the author/venue side to one row per paper (e.g., pick a canonical author row or aggregate authors into a list) before joining. This prevents accidental multiplication of edge rows.

views.description: One-row-per-citation relation linking citing and cited papers with their titles (when available). Use for citation network queries, counting in/out-degree, or tracing citation neighborhoods. | Use for: Build citation networks; Count citations given/received per paper; Find neighbors of a paper in the citation graph

views.name: papers_per_author_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT a.authorId, a.authorName, COUNT(w.paperId) AS paper_count, MAX(p.year) AS most_recent_year
FROM author a
LEFT JOIN writes w ON a.authorId = w.authorId
LEFT JOIN paper p ON w.paperId = p.paperId
GROUP BY a.authorId, a.authorName

params.description: Per-author aggregates: total papers authored and the most recent paper year for each author.
params.when_to_use: Get the total number of papers and latest publication year for each author. | Rank or filter authors by productivity (paper_count) or recency (most_recent_year). | Join author-level metrics to author dimension data when building author-level reports or dashboards. | Serve as the aggregated input when composing higher-level metrics (for example, authors per venue after joining to venue-level aggregates) provided joins are cardinality-safe.
params.output_schema: authorId: unique identifier of the author (from author.authorId). This is the GROUP BY key for the view. | authorName: display name of the author (from author.authorName). This is included in the GROUP BY and represents the author's name at aggregation time. | paper_count: count of distinct write relationships (COUNT(w.paperId) as computed in the view). Derived from the writes.paperId occurrences joined to author; represents how many papers are associated with the author according to the writes table. | most_recent_year: latest publication year among papers associated with the author (MAX(p.year)). Derived from paper.year via the writes -> paper join; NULL if the author has no papers.
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(writes.paperId) -- counts rows in writes for this author after LEFT JOIN; counts NULL-excluded write.paperId occurrences so authors with no writes yield 0 (depending on SQL dialect COUNT returns 0 when grouped but no matching rows are present due to LEFT JOIN then COUNT yields 0). | most_recent_year = MAX(paper.year) -- maximum year across joined paper rows for this author; returns NULL for authors with no matched papers.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to an author dimension (author table or any one-row-per-author view) on authorId — safe because papers_per_author_agg is one-row-per-author (grain ['authorId','authorName']), so joining a one-row-per-author dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to ranked or aggregated author-level views (for example author_paper_counts_ranked) on authorId — safe because both sides are author-grain and will not multiply paper_count or most_recent_year. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables or views (for example paper_base, paper_with_venue_journal, paper_authors, paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, citation_edges, paper_citation_counts_agg) without re-aggregating or deduplicating first — these are one-to-many relative to author and will multiply paper_count and distort most_recent_year unless you aggregate the child side to author grain before joining. | If you need author metrics combined with paper-level details, join papers_per_author_agg to the paper table on authorId and paperId only after aggregating or windowing the paper side appropriately (for example, join to a deduplicated subquery of papers or to a per-author-per-paper distinct set). This prevents double-counting write relationships. | When joining to other author-aggregates (e.g., papers_per_venue_agg which is aggregated per venue), ensure the join keys are authorId (or another author-level key) and that the other view is also author-grain; if the other view is per-venue, do not join directly unless you first aggregate/join via an intermediate mapping that is one-row-per-author (for example, author->venue mapping aggregated to author). | To incorporate dataset-, keyphrase-, or citation-based counts per author, first compute those measures at author grain (aggregate the one-to-many tables by authorId) and then join to this view on authorId; do not join the raw one-to-many sources directly.

views.description: Aggregate counts of papers per author (one row per author) and the most recent paper year. Useful for author productivity summaries and trend baselines. | Use for: Rank or filter authors by productivity; Find active authors (by most_recent_year) and their paper counts; Join to author dimension for further analysis

views.name: papers_per_venue_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT v.venueId, v.venueName, COUNT(p.paperId) AS paper_count, AVG(p.numCiting) AS avg_numCiting, AVG(p.numCitedBy) AS avg_numCitedBy
FROM venue v
LEFT JOIN paper p ON p.venueId = v.venueId
GROUP BY v.venueId, v.venueName

params.description: Aggregated counts and average citation statistics of papers per venue (one row per venue).
params.when_to_use: Get the number of papers and average citation metrics for each venue (e.g., leaderboards, reports by venue). | Join venue-level metrics into dashboards or analyses that are also at venue grain without re-aggregation. | Compose higher-level analytics that compare venues (e.g., rank venues by paper_count or avg_numCiting). | As a pre-aggregated source when combining venue metrics with other single-row-per-venue dimensions (e.g., venue metadata).
params.output_schema: venueId: identifier of the venue; derived from venue.venueId (base table column). | venueName: human-readable name of the venue; derived from venue.venueName (base table column). | paper_count: number of papers assigned to this venue; derived as COUNT(paper.paperId) over paper rows joined to the venue (aggregate). | avg_numCiting: average of paper.numCiting for papers in this venue; derived as AVG(paper.numCiting) (aggregate). | avg_numCitedBy: average of paper.numCitedBy for papers in this venue; derived as AVG(paper.numCitedBy) (aggregate).
params.grounded_columns: venue.venueId | venue.venueName | paper.paperId | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy | paper.venueId
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(paper.paperId)  -- count of paper rows associated with the venue (NULL-safe because LEFT JOIN counts only matched paper.paperId values). | avg_numCiting = AVG(paper.numCiting)  -- arithmetic mean of the numCiting values for papers in the venue. | avg_numCitedBy = AVG(paper.numCitedBy)  -- arithmetic mean of the numCitedBy values for papers in the venue.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to the venue dimension (e.g., venue table or any other view that is one-row-per-venue keyed by venueId) on venueId — safe because papers_per_venue_agg is one row per venue, so its measures are not duplicated when joined to another one-row-per-venue relation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling aggregate views that are also one-row-per-venue (if present) on venueId — safe for the same reason (both sides are at venue grain). | do NOT directly join papers_per_venue_agg to one-to-many tables or joins (for example paper_authors, paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, citation_edges, or paper-level JOIN views) without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply the venue-level measures because those tables have multiple rows per paper (and therefore multiple rows per venue). If you need to combine with one-to-many detail, either: | - aggregate the detail up to venueId before joining (e.g., compute counts or other aggregates grouped by paper.venueId), or | - join on a one-row-per-venue view/dimension and then derive combined metrics from those aggregated inputs. | When composing with other aggregates (e.g., papers_per_author_agg or paper_citation_counts_agg), ensure the other side is aggregated to venue-level (grouped by venueId) before joining, otherwise re-aggregate after the join to avoid duplicating paper_count and average metrics. | Safe keys: venueId is the canonical join key. Joins on venueName are not recommended as they may not be unique. | Rationale: The view groups by venue.venueId, venue.venueName producing exactly one row per venue present in the venue table. Any join partner that is also one-row-per-venue preserves that cardinality; any partner with many rows per venue will multiply this view's aggregates unless those partner rows are pre-aggregated to venue granularity.

views.description: Counts of papers per venue with average citation measures (one row per venue). Useful for venue-level summaries and comparing citation impact across venues. | Use for: Compare venues by paper volume or citation averages; Filter venues by minimum paper_count (downstream); Trend venue impact when joined with year buckets

views.name: author_paper_counts_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT ap.authorId, ap.authorName, ap.paper_count, ap.most_recent_year, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ap.paper_count DESC) AS productivity_rank
FROM (SELECT a.authorId, a.authorName, COUNT(w.paperId) AS paper_count, MAX(p.year) AS most_recent_year
      FROM author a
      LEFT JOIN writes w ON a.authorId = w.authorId
      LEFT JOIN paper p ON w.paperId = p.paperId
      GROUP BY a.authorId, a.authorName) ap

params.description: Ranks authors by their total paper counts and reports each author's paper count and most recent publication year.
params.when_to_use: Find the number of papers written by each author and their relative productivity rank (dense rank) across all authors. | List authors ordered by productivity to identify top contributors. | Compose author-level reports or dashboards that need paper_count, most_recent_year, and a stable productivity rank. | As a building block for joins where you need one row per author with pre-aggregated paper metrics (e.g., to attach author profile info or further author-level metrics).
params.output_schema: authorId: Unique identifier for the author. Derived from base column author.authorId (GROUP BY key). | authorName: Author's name as stored in the author table. Derived from base column author.authorName (GROUP BY key). | paper_count: Number of distinct write relationships (papers) associated with the author within the joined data. Derived as COUNT(w.paperId) in the inner aggregation. | most_recent_year: The maximum paper year across papers the author wrote. Derived as MAX(p.year) in the inner aggregation. | productivity_rank: Dense rank of authors ordered by paper_count descending. Derived as DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ap.paper_count DESC) computed over the aggregated author rows.
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(w.paperId)  -- count of writes.paperId per author (authors with zero writes yield 0 due to LEFT JOIN aggregate semantics) | most_recent_year = MAX(p.year)  -- most recent paper.year per author (NULL if author has no papers) | productivity_rank = DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY paper_count DESC)  -- dense ranking of authors by paper_count
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author (or any one-row-per-author dimension) on authorId — safe because this view has exactly one row per authorId (grain = ['authorId']), so measures (paper_count, most_recent_year, productivity_rank) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to papers_per_author_agg (AGG) on authorId — safe only if that sibling aggregate is also one-row-per-author and contains complementary pre-aggregated metrics; joining two one-row-per-author sources preserves correct measures. | DO NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child table or view (for example paper_authors, paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, citation_edges, paper_with_venue_journal when expanded to multiple rows per paper, or any raw paper-level table) without re-aggregation. Those joins will multiplicatively duplicate paper_count and will make productivity_rank and aggregate measures incorrect. | If you must attach information from a one-to-many relation (e.g., datasets used by an author's papers), first aggregate that relation to one row per author (for example: count of distinct datasets per author) and then join the aggregated result to this view on authorId — this preserves cardinality and keeps paper_count and productivity_rank correct. | When joining to sibling aggregates that are at a different grain (e.g., papers_per_venue_agg), ensure you join via an appropriate key and/or aggregate to author grain first. Do not rely on database-level implicit de-duplication. | This view is safe to use as the right-hand side of a join when the left side is one-row-per-author (profile tables, author-level metadata). If used in analytical pipelines, treat paper_count and productivity_rank as author-level measures and re-aggregate after any join that may introduce multiplicity.

views.description: Authors ranked by paper_count with a dense rank. One row per author. Use this CTE when selecting top-k authors by productivity via WHERE rank <= K downstream. | Use for: Select top-K authors by number of papers (use WHERE productivity_rank <= K); Compare authors with same paper_count (dense rank handles ties); Combine rank with recent activity filters

views.name: paper_citation_counts_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.paperId, COALESCE(in_c.count_in,0) AS inbound_citation_count, COALESCE(out_c.count_out,0) AS outbound_citation_count
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT paperId FROM paper) p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT citedPaperId AS paperId, COUNT(*) AS count_in
  FROM cite
  GROUP BY citedPaperId
) in_c ON p.paperId = in_c.paperId
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT citingPaperId AS paperId, COUNT(*) AS count_out
  FROM cite
  GROUP BY citingPaperId
) out_c ON p.paperId = out_c.paperId

params.description: Per-paper counts of inbound (times cited) and outbound (references made) citations — one row per paperId.
params.when_to_use: Get how many times a paper has been cited (inbound) and how many references it contains (outbound). | Joinable per-paper summary when building higher-level metrics (e.g., average citations per venue, per-author aggregates) without re-counting citation rows. | Filtering/ranking papers by citation counts (top cited, most outgoing references). | Composing with other paper-level attributes (title, venue, authors, keyphrases) while preserving correct counts.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for a paper; derived from paper.paperId (distinct list of paper IDs from the base paper table). | inbound_citation_count: number of rows in cite where cite.citedPaperId = paperId (COALESCE(in_c.count_in, 0)); derived from COUNT(*) grouped by cite.citedPaperId. | outbound_citation_count: number of rows in cite where cite.citingPaperId = paperId (COALESCE(out_c.count_out, 0)); derived from COUNT(*) grouped by cite.citingPaperId.
params.metric: inbound_citation_count = COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cite WHERE cite.citedPaperId = paper.paperId GROUP BY cite.citedPaperId), 0) | outbound_citation_count = COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cite WHERE cite.citingPaperId = paper.paperId GROUP BY cite.citingPaperId), 0)
params.composition: Join to paper_base (or any other paper-level JOIN view such as paper_with_venue_journal, paper_authors (when reduced to one row per paper), paper_datasets (when reduced), paper_keyphrases (when reduced)) on paperId — safe because paper_citation_counts_agg is one-row-per-paperId, so its measures are not duplicated when joined to another one-row-per-paper relation. | Join to author-level aggregates (for example authors -> papers aggregated) by first aggregating or joining through a one-row-per-paper mapping (e.g., join paper_citation_counts_agg to paper_author mapping that is one-row-per-paper-author only if the downstream planner re-aggregates counts appropriately). Prefer joining through pre-aggregated author-level views (like papers_per_author_agg) to avoid duplicating counts. | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views (for example citation_edges, paper_authors, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets) that are one-to-many from paperId without re-aggregation, because each matching child row would duplicate inbound_citation_count and outbound_citation_count. Instead either: | - aggregate the child table to one row per paperId before joining, or | - join and then re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(inbound_citation_count) grouped by the desired key) taking care to deduplicate paper-level measures if needed. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (venue-level, author-level): compute SUM(inbound_citation_count) and SUM(outbound_citation_count) over paperId, joining on paperId to a one-row-per-paper relation; this preserves correct totals because paper_citation_counts_agg already provides per-paper totals.

views.description: Per-paper incoming and outgoing citation counts computed from the cite table (one row per paper). Prefer this to rely on citation edges in cite rather than numCiting/numCitedBy columns if those summaries may be stale. | Use for: Find most-cited papers by inbound_citation_count; Compare reported numCitedBy/numCiting to computed counts; Filter papers with zero inbound or outbound citations

views.name: author_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  TRIM(author.authorName) AS authorName
FROM author

params.description: Provides a cleaned identity row per author: the author's ID and trimmed display name.
params.when_to_use: Lookup an author's canonical name by authorId. | Join author identity to other tables/views to annotate rows with authorName. | Use as a dimension when aggregating metrics per author (author-level reporting). | Compose into larger queries that need a single row per author (e.g., join to author-level aggregates).
params.output_schema: authorId: unique identifier for an author; derives from base column author.authorId | authorName: normalized/trimmed author display name; derives from TRIM(author.authorName) (base column author.authorName)
params.metric: authorId = author.authorId | authorName = TRIM(author.authorName)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to papers_per_author_agg on authorId — safe because papers_per_author_agg is an aggregation at the same grain (one row per author) so joining preserves one-row-per-author and does not duplicate author-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_paper_counts_ranked on authorId — safe because that view is author-scoped/ranked (one row per author or one row per author per rank depending on its grain); only safe when that view's grain is one row per author. If it contains multiple rows per author (e.g., ranked items), treat it as one-to-many. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity on authorId from any view that is at paper-level (e.g., paper_base, paper_with_venue_journal, paper_authors, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges) — safe when you intend to annotate each paper-row with its authorName. This is one-to-many from author_identity to paper-level rows but does NOT duplicate author_identity's measures because author_identity contains one row per author; however joining author_identity onto a many-row-per-author set will increase result rows proportional to that set (this is expected for annotation). | do NOT join author_identity to a one-to-many detail without re-aggregating first: for example, do NOT join author_identity to paper_authors (which is one-to-many from author to papers) and then sum author-level metrics from author_identity without re-aggregation, because paper_authors will multiply rows per author. Instead, either (a) aggregate the detail to author-level first (e.g., papers_per_author_agg) and then join, or (b) perform distinct/GROUP BY on authorId after joining to restore one row per author. | do NOT assume joins to multi-row sibling views (paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges) preserve author-level cardinality — these are one-to-many from author (via paper) and will duplicate author rows if not aggregated. Re-aggregate after such joins if you need author-level measures. | general rule: this view is strictly one-row-per author (grain = ['author.authorId']). Any join that preserves that one-row-per-author mapping (other one-row-per-author views or pre-aggregated author-level metrics) is safe; joins to tables/views with more than one row per author require aggregation or de-duplication to avoid multiplying author-level measures.

views.description: Provides a cleaned identity row per author: the author's ID and trimmed display name.
validated_on: Identify all distinct paper IDs for works that have been co-authored by both Peter Mertens and Dina Barbian.

views.name: paper_authorship
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  writes.paperId AS paperId,
  writes.authorId AS authorId
FROM writes

params.description: Lists the (paperId, authorId) pairs representing each authorship relationship (which authors wrote which papers).
params.when_to_use: Enumerating authors for a given paper or papers | Enumerating papers for a given author or authors | Joining authorship links to other paper- or author-level attributes (e.g., paper metadata, author identity) without changing the one-row-per-authorship grain | As a base to aggregate counts (e.g., papers per author, authors per paper) by composing higher-level aggregations
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from writes.paperId | authorId: identifier of the author — derived from writes.authorId
params.metric: No derived numeric metrics in this view; it is a pure relational projection at the authorship grain. Aggregate metrics should be computed by aggregating rows from this view, for example: | papers_per_author = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) GROUP BY authorId | authors_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) GROUP BY paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity on authorId — safe because author_identity is a normalized (one-row-per-author) table/view so joining will not duplicate authorship rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (or paper_with_venue_journal) on paperId — safe because those are normalized one-row-per-paper views, so joining preserves the one-row-per-authorship grain and does not multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_citation_counts_agg on paperId — safe because paper_citation_counts_agg is an aggregate at the paper grain (one row per paper), so measures computed from authorship (e.g., counting rows) remain correct when combined. | do NOT naively join to paper_authors (JOIN) or other one-to-many siblings (e.g., paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets) without re-aggregation — these are one-to-many relative to paper (or to authorship) and would multiply authorship rows and therefore inflate any row-count-based measures unless you first aggregate them to a compatible grain. Instead, aggregate the many-side to one-row-per-paper or one-row-per-author before joining. | do NOT join to papers_per_author_agg or author_paper_counts_ranked expecting additional multiplicative detail — these are already aggregated/ranked views and should be used as lookup/join targets only when their grain matches the intended result (e.g., join papers_per_author_agg to authorId after ensuring you are aggregating authorship rows to author-level). | When composing metrics: compute aggregations explicitly from this view (e.g., COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY authorId) to get papers per author) or aggregate to the desired grain before joining to other one-to-many datasets to avoid row multiplication.

views.description: Lists the (paperId, authorId) pairs representing each authorship relationship (which authors wrote which papers).
validated_on: Hey there! Can you help me find all the papers that were co-authored by Dina Barbian and Peter Mertens? I'd love to know their unique paper IDs!

views.name: paper_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paper.paperId AS paperId,
  paper.title AS title,
  paper.venueId AS venueId,
  paper.year AS year,
  paper.numCiting AS numCiting,
  paper.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy,
  paper.journalId AS journalId
FROM paper

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper basic attributes and counts (paper id, title, venue/journal identifiers, year, and citation counts).
params.when_to_use: Fetch core paper metadata for a single paper or a set of papers (title, year, venueId, journalId). | Start point for composing additional aggregates or joins about papers (e.g., attach authors, keyphrases, datasets, citation aggregates). | Filter or group by paper attributes (year, venueId, journalId) before joining to other dimensions or aggregates.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for a paper — derives from table column paper.paperId | title: paper title string — derives from table column paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper was presented/published — derives from table column paper.venueId | year: publication year of the paper — derives from table column paper.year | numCiting: number of outgoing citations from this paper (how many other papers this paper cites) — derives from table column paper.numCiting | numCitedBy: number of incoming citations to this paper (how many other papers cite this paper) — derives from table column paper.numCitedBy | journalId: identifier of the journal (if any) for this paper — derives from table column paper.journalId
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy | paper.journalId
params.metric: numCiting = paper.numCiting (base column, stored count of outgoing citations for that paper) | numCitedBy = paper.numCitedBy (base column, stored count of incoming citations for that paper)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (NORM) on paperId — safe because both represent the same one-row-per-paper grain, so measures from paper_basic are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity (NORM) only via pre-aggregated author-level views or via the paper_authorship view with an aggregation step — do NOT directly inner-join paper_basic to paper_authorship (a one-to-many table) without aggregating authors per paper first, because paper_authorship is many authors per paper and would multiply numCiting/numCitedBy if not re-aggregated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_with_venue_journal (JOIN) on paperId — safe if that view is implemented as one-row-per-paper (it is sibling JOIN), because it preserves the one-row-per-paper grain; verify it does not expand to multiple rows per paper. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many siblings such as paper_authors, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges without re-aggregation first — these views/tables are many-rows-per-paper and will duplicate paper_basic measures (numCiting, numCitedBy) unless you re-aggregate the result back to paperId (for example, count authors per paper, then join). | safe composition pattern: to attach author counts, use papers_per_author_agg (AGG) or compute an aggregated subquery that yields one row per paper (e.g., COUNT(*) AS author_count GROUP BY paperId) and then join on paperId — this preserves cardinality. | safe composition pattern: to incorporate citation-based aggregates from paper_citation_counts_agg (AGG), join on paperId only if that aggregation is one-row-per-paper; otherwise aggregate citation_edges to paper-level before joining. | when joining to ranked or aggregated views (author_paper_counts_ranked, papers_per_venue_agg, paper_citation_counts_agg), ensure the target view is one-row-per-paper or one-row-per-key you desire; if it is one-to-many relative to paper_basic, aggregate first to paperId to avoid measure duplication.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-paper basic attributes and counts (paper id, title, venue/journal identifiers, year, and citation counts).

views.name: paper_impact_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.numCiting,
  CASE
    WHEN p.numCiting IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN p.numCiting = 0 THEN 'low'
    WHEN p.numCiting BETWEEN 1 AND 10 THEN 'medium'
    WHEN p.numCiting BETWEEN 11 AND 100 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'very_high'
  END AS impact_label
FROM paper_base p

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper counts of how many other papers cite the paper and a categorical impact label derived from that count.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve a paper's citation count and human-readable impact category | Filter or group papers by impact category (unknown/low/medium/high/very_high) | Join into higher-level aggregations per author/venue when starting from one-row-per-paper grain | Compose into dashboards, reports, or downstream queries that need a paper-level metric without re-aggregating citations
params.output_schema: paperId: paper primary identifier (derived from paper_base.paperId) | numCiting: count of citing papers as stored on the base paper record (derived from paper_base.numCiting) | impact_label: categorical label mapped from numCiting values with the following mapping - NULL -> 'unknown', 0 -> 'low', 1-10 -> 'medium', 11-100 -> 'high', >100 -> 'very_high' (derived from CASE expression on paper_base.numCiting)
params.metric: numCiting = paper_base.numCiting (precomputed citation count stored on the normalized paper_base row) | impact_label = CASE WHEN paper_base.numCiting IS NULL THEN 'unknown' WHEN paper_base.numCiting = 0 THEN 'low' WHEN paper_base.numCiting BETWEEN 1 AND 10 THEN 'medium' WHEN paper_base.numCiting BETWEEN 11 AND 100 THEN 'high' ELSE 'very_high' END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity on paperId via a pre-aggregated or one-row-per-paper authorship mapping (for example join to a papers_per_author_agg or a paper_authorship view that is one-row-per-paper-per-author only when you plan to re-aggregate) — safe because this view is one-row-per-paper and joining to a one-row-per-paper dimension (e.g., paper_base or normalized paper metadata) will not duplicate measures | safe: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe because paper_with_venue_journal is a one-row-per-paper enriched join (does not multiply rows) so numCiting remains correct | safe: join to papers_per_venue_agg or papers_per_author_agg when those aggregates are keyed by venue or author respectively and you aggregate after joining (join must be followed by grouping by the aggregate key to avoid duplication of paper-level rows) | do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views such as paper_authors, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges, or paper_authorship if they are one-row-per-(paper,thing) because joining directly will duplicate this view's paper rows and thus multiply numCiting and distort derived counts. If you must join to such one-to-many detail, either: | - re-aggregate the detail back to one-row-per-paper before joining (e.g., count keyphrases per paper, then join), or | - perform the join at the paper-level and then use DISTINCT or GROUP BY paperId to re-establish one-row-per-paper and use an appropriate aggregation (e.g., MAX(numCiting) or MIN/ANY_VALUE) to preserve the paper-level measure correctly. | example safe composition patterns: | - To compute average citation count per author: start from paper_impact_category (one row per paper), join to paper_authorship (one-to-many) then GROUP BY authorId and compute AVG(numCiting) — because you re-aggregate after the join, duplication is handled correctly. | - To attach venue fields: join paper_impact_category -> paper_with_venue_journal on paperId and then aggregate by venueId without re-aggregation of paper rows (one-to-one join).

views.description: Provides one-row-per-paper counts of how many other papers cite the paper and a categorical impact label derived from that count.

  author.authorId AS authorId,
  author.authorName AS authorName
FROM author

params.description: Provides the canonical identity for each author (authorId -> authorName).
params.when_to_use: Look up an author's display name given authorId | Serve as the author dimension when counting or aggregating measures per author | Join to author-level aggregated metrics (e.g., papers per author, citation counts per author) to add readable authorName | Compose into larger queries that need one-row-per-author context or to filter/select authors by id or name

params.metric: There are no aggregate metrics defined in this view; both outputs are direct columns: authorId = author.authorId, authorName = author.authorName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to this view on authorId from any aggregated author-level view/table (for example papers_per_author_agg, paper_citation_counts_agg, author_paper_counts_ranked) — safe because author_identity_14 is one-row-per-author (grain = ['authorId']) so joining these aggregated results to this view will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other one-row-per-author dimensions (for example author_identity or any normalized author table) on authorId — safe because both sides are one-row-per-author. | do NOT join author_identity_14 directly to one-to-many tables/views that list multiple papers, keyphrases, datasets, or citation edges (for example paper_authorship, paper_base, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges) without first aggregating or de-duplicating the many-side by author. Such joins would multiply author rows and therefore would duplicate any measures that assume one row per author. | If you need measures from one-to-many sources at the author grain, first aggregate those sources to authorId (for example: COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) per author in papers_per_author_agg) and then join the aggregated result to author_identity_14 on authorId to preserve correct counts. | When composing further joins, preserve author_identity_14 as the dimension (one row per author) or ensure the planner re-aggregates post-join back to authorId to maintain correct cardinality and avoid measure inflation.

views.description: Provides the canonical identity for each author (authorId -> authorName).

views.name: author_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  authorId,
  TRIM(authorName) AS authorName
FROM author

params.description: Canonical normalized author rows: one row per authorId with a trimmed authorName.
params.when_to_use: Lookup an author's display name given authorId | Join author identity information into paper- or citation-level queries when you need a single row per author | Serve as the canonical author dimension when composing aggregations by author (e.g., counts or sums computed from other tables) | Normalize authorName whitespace for presentation or grouping
params.output_schema: authorId: unique identifier for the author — sourced from author.authorId | authorName: trimmed display name for the author (leading/trailing whitespace removed) — derived from TRIM(author.authorName) in the author table

params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic metadata for a single paper or a set of papers by paperId. | Serve as the foundational layer when composing joins to enrich paper metadata (venues, journals, authors, metrics). | Use when building aggregations grouped by paper (e.g., citations per paper) or when joining into author/venue-level aggregates while preserving paper-level grain.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for the paper, derived from base table column paper.paperId | title: paper title text, derived from base table column paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper was presented/published, derived from base table column paper.venueId | journalId: identifier of the journal (if any) for the paper, derived from base table column paper.journalId | year: publication year of the paper, derived from base table column paper.year
params.metric: No derived aggregates or computed metrics in this view; all outputs are direct base columns: paperId = paper.paperId, title = paper.title, venueId = paper.venueId, journalId = paper.journalId, year = paper.year
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension views/tables that are one-to-one with paper at paper-level without re-aggregation — safe examples: |   - join to paper_base (NORM) on paperId — safe because both are one-row-per-paper (no duplication). |   - join to paper_with_venue_journal (JOIN) on paperId — safe when that view is one-row-per-paper (it enriches the same grain). |   - join to author_identity (NORM) on authorId only after connecting through a one-row-per-paper authorship relation (see unsafe guidance below). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many children without re-aggregation or deduplication first, because such joins will multiply this view's paper-level rows and thus duplicate any measures or counts derived at the paper grain. Unsafe examples requiring care: |   - do NOT join directly to paper_authors (JOIN) on paperId if paper_authors contains one row per (paper,author) — this is a one-to-many relation and will duplicate paper rows. Instead aggregate authors to one row per paper (e.g., array_agg(authorId) or count(*) grouped by paperId) before joining, or join using lateral subquery that returns a single composite column. |   - do NOT join directly to paper_datasets (JOIN), paper_keyphrases (JOIN), citation_edges (JOIN) if they are modeled one-to-many (e.g., multiple datasets/keyphrases/citation edges per paper). Re-aggregate those tables to paper-level (counts, lists) before joining. |   - when combining with aggregates (paper_citation_counts_agg, papers_per_author_agg, papers_per_venue_agg, paper_authorship, paper_citation_counts_agg), ensure you join on paperId or the appropriate key where the aggregate is already computed at paper grain; joining to an aggregate that is at a different grain is allowed only if the aggregate's grain matches this view's grain (paperId) or you re-aggregate accordingly. | General rule for planners: treat this view as strictly one-row-per-paper (key = paperId). Any join to a table/view that is one-to-one on paperId will not duplicate rows; any join to a one-to-many relation must be pre-aggregated/deduplicated to one row per paperId to preserve correct counts/measures.

views.name: paper_authors_25

SELECT w.paperId AS paperId,
       w.authorId AS authorId,
       a.authorName AS authorName,

FROM writes AS w
JOIN author AS a ON w.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: Provides one row per (paper, author) listing the paper id, author id, author name, paper title and paper citation count (numCitedBy).
params.when_to_use: List authors on a paper along with paper metadata (title, citation count). | Filter or search papers by author or authors by paper and return citation counts for those paper-author pairs. | Compose into higher-level aggregations such as counts of papers per author, total citations per author (when aggregated), or author-by-paper reporting. | Joinable as a detail (fact-like) layer when building author–paper level reports or dashboards.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — identifier of the paper (sourced from writes.paperId which references paper.paperId) | authorId: writes.authorId / author.authorId — identifier of the author (sourced from writes.authorId which references author.authorId) | authorName: author.authorName — the canonical display name of the author from the author table | title: paper.title — the paper's title from the paper table | numCitedBy: paper.numCitedBy — paper's citation count metric stored on the paper table
params.grounded_columns: writes.paperId | writes.authorId | author.authorId | author.authorName | paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.numCitedBy
params.metric: numCitedBy = direct column copy of paper.numCitedBy (no aggregation performed in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity (or author) on authorId — safe because this view already has a single row per (paperId, authorId) and author_identity is one-row-per-author, so measures (numCitedBy) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base or paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe because those are one-row-per-paper dimension/normalized views; joining preserves one row per (paperId, authorId) and does not multiply numCitedBy. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children of paper (for example paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, paper_authorship, or citation_edges) without re-aggregation first — those are one-to-many from paper and would multiply rows per (paperId, authorId) and thereby duplicate paper-level measures like numCitedBy unless you aggregate the one-to-many side first (e.g., aggregate datasets per paper, keyphrases per paper, or edges per paper to counts) or otherwise deduplicate. | do NOT join directly to papers_per_author_agg or author_paper_counts_ranked expecting row-level preservation — those are aggregated/ranked outputs; if you need aggregated metrics per author, join on authorId but be aware those views provide summary-level metrics and will change grain (one-row-per-author). | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total citations per author), aggregate numCitedBy grouped by authorId after selecting from this view (e.g., SUM(numCitedBy) GROUP BY authorId). This prevents accidental duplication: always aggregate after joining any one-to-many detail. | If you need to attach multiple one-to-many dimensions (e.g., datasets and keyphrases) to this view, first aggregate each one-to-many dimension to paper-level summaries, then join those aggregated results on paperId to avoid Cartesian multiplication of rows.
