views.name: papers_with_author_names_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COALESCE(pa.author_count, 0) AS author_count,
  COALESCE(pa.author_names_concat, '') AS author_names_list,
  p.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy
FROM paper_base p
LEFT JOIN paper_coauthors_agg pa ON p.paperId = pa.paperId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper with the paper's id, the count of its authors, a concatenated list of its author names, and the paper's citation count (numCitedBy).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic paper-level metadata including how many authors and their names alongside citation count. | Compose further aggregations at the paper-level (e.g., ranking papers by citations or filtering papers by author_count). | Join paper-level attributes into downstream analyses where each paper must remain one row (e.g., joining to venues, datasets, or keyphrases after respecting cardinality rules).
params.output_schema: paperId: unique paper identifier; derived from paper_base.paperId (base table). | author_count: number of distinct authors for the paper; derived from paper_coauthors_agg.author_count (aggregated source). If NULL in source, 0 is used. | author_names_list: authors' names concatenated for the paper; derived from paper_coauthors_agg.author_names_concat (aggregated source). If NULL in source, empty string is used. | numCitedBy: citation count for the paper; derived from paper_base.numCitedBy (base table).
params.metric: author_count = COALESCE(paper_coauthors_agg.author_count, 0) -- sourced aggregate: count of authors per paper computed in paper_coauthors_agg | author_names_list = COALESCE(paper_coauthors_agg.author_names_concat, '') -- sourced aggregate: concatenated author names per paper in paper_coauthors_agg | numCitedBy = paper_base.numCitedBy -- base column representing number of citations
params.composition: Safe joins (won't duplicate this view's per-paper measures): join to one-row-per-paper or higher-grain dimensions on paperId. Example: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe because paper_with_venue_journal is a one-row-per-paper view (JOIN) and therefore does not multiply rows. | Safe joins to one-row-per-venue/one-row-per-author aggregates on their key when joining by that key after appropriate key mapping (e.g., join paper_per_venue_agg on venueId if you first have venueId from a one-row-per-paper source). | Do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables/views keyed by paperId without re-aggregation first. Examples to avoid: paper_authorship (JOIN), paper_datasets (JOIN), paper_keyphrases (JOIN), citation_edges (JOIN) — these are one-to-many from paperId and will multiply rows and duplicate author_count/author_names_list/numCitedBy unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you must combine with one-to-many child tables (datasets, keyphrases, authorship rows, citation_edges), either: (a) aggregate the child side to one row per paper (e.g., COUNT, ARRAY_AGG, STRING_AGG grouped by paperId) and then join to this view on paperId; or (b) join first and then compute final aggregates over paperId so you re-compute measures at the correct grain. | This view is one-row-per-paper (grain = paperId). Any planner or downstream query should preserve that grain when composing: join only to other one-row-per-paper sources directly, or pre-aggregate many-side relations to paperId before joining, to ensure metrics (author_count, author_names_list, numCitedBy) are not inflated by row multiplication.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-paper with the paper's id, the count of its authors, a concatenated list of its author names, and the paper's citation count (numCitedBy).

views.name: paper_dataset_associations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paper_datasets.paperId AS paperId,
  paper_base.title AS title,
  paper_datasets.datasetId AS datasetId
FROM paper_datasets
JOIN paper_base ON paper_datasets.paperId = paper_base.paperId

params.description: All paper–dataset associations with the paper title — one row per (paperId, datasetId).
params.when_to_use: List datasets referenced/used by each paper (paperId → datasetId) along with the paper title. | Filter or aggregate datasets per paper (e.g., count datasets per paper) as a base relation for further analytics. | Join onto other paper-level analytics (citations, venue, authorship counts) without duplicating dataset associations when done correctly.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper identifier — derived from paper_datasets.paperId | title: paper title — derived from paper_base.title (joined by paperId) | datasetId: dataset identifier — derived from paper_datasets.datasetId
params.metric: This view is purely relational at the grain (paperId, datasetId); it defines no aggregated metrics. If you need a metric, compute it on top. Example derived metrics to compute externally: | datasets_per_paper = COUNT(datasetId) GROUP BY paperId | papers_per_dataset = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY datasetId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (or any other one-row-per-paper view like paper_with_venue_journal) on paperId — safe because this view is already one row per (paperId, datasetId) and paper_base is one row per paperId, so paper-level attributes will not multiply dataset associations. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_citation_counts_agg (aggregated per paperId) on paperId — safe because that aggregation is one row per paperId and will not duplicate rows; you can then compute ratios like citations per dataset by aggregating appropriately after the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to papers_per_venue_agg (aggregated per venue or paperId as appropriate) only when the agg is at the same key (paperId) or a coarser key and you intend to preserve the (paperId,datasetId) grain. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children of paper (e.g., paper_authors, paper_keyphrases, paper_authorship) without re-aggregation first — those are one-to-many relative to paperId and will multiply rows for a given (paperId, datasetId). If you need author-level detail alongside dataset associations, either: | - aggregate the child table to one row per paperId (e.g., authors_list, author_count) then join on paperId, or | - keep the join but then re-aggregate to the desired grain (paperId or paperId,datasetId) to remove duplication. | do NOT join to any non-aggregated table that contains multiple rows per paperId unless you intend to produce a multiplied cross-product (e.g., to get one row per (paperId, datasetId, authorId) that intentionally multiplies dimensions). | When composing metrics: compute aggregations at the view's grain (paperId,datasetId) or at paperId after collapsing dataset rows as needed to avoid accidental double-counting.

views.description: All paper–dataset associations with the paper title — one row per (paperId, datasetId).

views.name: paper_dataset_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pd.datasetId) AS dataset_count
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN paperDataset pd ON p.paperId = pd.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper count of distinct datasets referenced by each paper (one row per paper).
params.when_to_use: Report how many distinct datasets are associated with each paper (e.g., distribution, filtering papers that reference N datasets). | Join as a per-paper metric when computing paper-level summaries or rankings that use dataset_count. | Compose into higher-level aggregations (e.g., datasets per author, datasets per venue) by correctly aggregating dataset_count after safe joins.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the primary identifier for the paper (derived from paper table's paperId). | dataset_count: COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId) — number of distinct datasetId values associated with the paper (derived from paperDataset.datasetId aggregated via COUNT(DISTINCT)).
params.metric: dataset_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId) GROUPED BY paper.paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any one-row-per-paper dimension (for example a normalized paper row) on paperId — safe because paper_dataset_counts is aggregated at paperId (one row per paper), so joining to another one-row-per-paper view/table will not duplicate dataset_count. | Example safe joins: join to paper_base on paperId (one row per paper), join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId, join to paper_citation_counts_agg on paperId (if that view is also one-row-per-paper). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables/views on paperId (for example paper_authorship, paper_datasets [if that sibling is non-aggregated and repeats dataset rows], paper_keyphrases, citation_edges) without re-aggregation — such joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate dataset_count. If you must combine with a one-to-many relation, first aggregate that relation to one row per paper (or re-aggregate after the join) before combining metrics. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., datasets per author): either (a) join this view to an author-paper mapping that is one-row-per-paper-per-author and then SUM(dataset_count) after deduplicating papers per author as appropriate, or (b) re-compute dataset distinct counts from the underlying paperDataset table grouped at the target grain (e.g., authorId + paperId or authorId) to avoid double-counting when papers are linked to multiple authors. | If joining to another AGG view that is not at paperId grain, ensure that view is either also at paperId or at a coarser grain with aggregation semantics known; otherwise re-aggregate so measures remain correct.

views.description: Per-paper count of distinct datasets referenced by each paper (one row per paper).

views.name: paper_authors_distinct
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT paperId, authorId
FROM writes
WHERE paperId IS NOT NULL AND authorId IS NOT NULL

params.description: Distinct author-paper pairing: the set of unique (paperId, authorId) rows representing that an author wrote a paper.
params.when_to_use: Answering whether a specific author is credited on a given paper (existence of an authorship link). | Counting or listing authors per paper or papers per author when built as an aggregate on top of this view. | Joining paper-level or author-level attributes onto unique author↔paper links without duplicating authorship links. | As a cardinality-safe seed when composing further aggregates (e.g., papers-per-author, authors-per-paper) because it is normalized to one row per author-paper.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from writes.paperId (SELECT DISTINCT paperId, ...). | authorId: identifier of the author — derived from writes.authorId (SELECT DISTINCT ..., authorId).
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) over this view (interpreted as number of distinct author-paper links) = COUNT_DISTINCT(writes.paperId || '||' || writes.authorId) when computed on base table; when aggregating from this view use COUNT(*) to count links without double-counting. | papers_per_author(authorId) = COUNT(*) GROUP BY authorId when aggregating this view by authorId. | authors_per_paper(paperId) = COUNT(*) GROUP BY paperId when aggregating this view by paperId.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base on paperId — safe because this view has at most one row per (paperId, authorId); joining paper attributes (one row per paper) does not duplicate authorship links and preserves one row per author-paper. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity on authorId — safe because author_identity is expected to be one row per author (authorId). Joining author attributes will not duplicate the author-paper rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe for the same reason as paper_base; paper-level metadata can be attached without duplicating author-paper rows. | do NOT join (without re-aggregation) to one-to-many children of the paper or author such as paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, citation_edges, or paper_authorship if those tables/views are one-to-many relative to the paper or the author — such joins will multiply the author-paper rows and therefore multiply any counts/metrics derived from this view. | If you need to combine with one-to-many relations (e.g., attach datasets per paper) and keep measures from this view correct, either: (a) aggregate the child (e.g., count datasets per paper) to one row per paper and then join on paperId, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate back to the intended grain (paperId, authorId) or higher. | When composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., papers_per_author), compute them by aggregating this view (GROUP BY authorId) rather than joining this view to other one-to-many tables and then counting, to avoid accidental multiplication. | This view is normalized to grain [paperId, authorId]; any join that preserves or reduces grain by joining to one-row-per-key dimensions (paper or author) is safe. Any join that expands grain must be followed by aggregation to restore correct measure semantics.

views.description: Distinct author-paper pairing: the set of unique (paperId, authorId) rows representing that an author wrote a paper.

views.name: paper_author_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS num_distinct_authors
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: For each paper (paperId), the count of distinct authors who wrote that paper.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of distinct authors for a given paper or set of papers. | Filter or sort papers by how many distinct authors they have. | Compose with other per-paper aggregates (e.g., citation counts) to build metrics per paper. | Compute author-to-paper ratios when joined with per-author aggregates (with careful aggregation).
params.output_schema: paperId: the paper's unique identifier, derived from paper.paperId in the base table. | num_distinct_authors: the count of distinct authors for that paper, derived from COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) in the aggregate.
params.metric: num_distinct_authors = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) per paperId (aggregate computed in the view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or one-row-per-paper views/tables on paperId — e.g., join to paper_base on paperId — safe because paper_author_counts is one-row-per-paper and such joins are one-to-one, so num_distinct_authors is not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to other per-paper AGG views (paper_citation_counts_agg, papers_per_venue_agg when keyed by paperId) on paperId after ensuring those views are also one-row-per-paper — safe because both sides are aggregated to the same grain (paperId). | do NOT directly join to one-to-many children of paper (writes, paper_authorship, paper_keyphrases, paper_datasets, citation_edges, paper_with_venue_journal if it multiplies rows) without re-aggregating or deduplicating first, because those joins would multiply rows and thus multiply this view's measures. Instead, either: | - join this view to such one-to-many tables using a subquery/derived table that aggregates them to one row per paperId first, or | - re-aggregate after the join (e.g., GROUP BY paperId and recompute COUNT/other metrics) to restore correct counts. | do NOT join to author-level views (papers_per_author_agg, author_identity, author_paper_counts_ranked) on authorId directly without first ensuring aggregation is done at paperId — joining on authorId would cause fan-out from paper rows to multiple authors and duplicate num_distinct_authors unless you re-aggregate. | When composing with ranked or partitioned views (author_paper_counts_ranked), prefer joining through an intermediate per-paper or per-author aggregated view and then re-aggregating to the desired grain to avoid double-counting. | If you need per-paper-per-author detail, join the base writes table (or paper_authorship) and compute measures there; do not rely on this aggregate view for row-level joins since it has lost author-level detail (it only preserves the distinct count).

views.description: For each paper (paperId), the count of distinct authors who wrote that paper.

views.name: keyphrase_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  keyphraseId,
  keyphraseName
FROM keyphrase

params.description: Provides one-row-per-keyphrase identifiers and their canonical names, useful as a normalized dimension of keyphrases.
params.when_to_use: Lookup keyphrase metadata (id -> name) when reporting on metrics grouped by keyphraseId or keyphraseName. | Joining to aggregated measures that are computed at the keyphrase grain (e.g., counts of papers per keyphrase) to add readable names. | Composing additional SQL that needs a stable keyphrase dimension (filtering, labeling, or joining by keyphraseId).
params.output_schema: keyphraseId: unique identifier for the keyphrase — derived from base column keyphrase.keyphraseId | keyphraseName: canonical display name of the keyphrase — derived from base column keyphrase.keyphraseName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or aggregate views on keyphraseId — safe examples: |   - Join to paper_keyphrases on keyphraseId — safe when paper_keyphrases is an association (many papers to one keyphrase) but you should treat paper_keyphrases as a fact/relationship and aggregate there; joining this view (one-row-per-keyphrase) to an already-aggregated per-keyphrase metric on keyphraseId will NOT duplicate the aggregated measures. |   - Join to any per-keyphrase aggregate (e.g., a hypothetical papers_per_keyphrase_agg) on keyphraseId — safe because keyphrase_row is one-row-per-keyphrase, so it will not multiply rows of a result already aggregated to keyphraseId. | Do NOT join cardinality-unsafe (would multiply rows) without re-aggregation: |   - Do NOT directly join keyphrase_row to one-to-many child tables (e.g., paper_base, paper_authors, paper_datasets, citation_edges) on keyphraseId unless you intend to expand to paper-level detail. Those joins will duplicate the keyphrase row for each matching paper/author/dataset/citation and will multiply any measures derived from keyphrase_row. |   - If you need measures that combine keyphrase metadata with counts or metrics from one-to-many tables, first aggregate the many-side to one row per keyphraseId (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) AS papers_for_keyphrase grouped by keyphraseId) and then join that aggregate to keyphrase_row on keyphraseId — this preserves correct cardinality. | General rule: keyphrase_row is a dimension (NORM) with grain = keyphraseId. It is safe to join it into analyses that are already at keyphrase grain; avoid joining it into lower-grain (paper-level) queries unless you accept row expansion or re-aggregate afterwards.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-keyphrase identifiers and their canonical names, useful as a normalized dimension of keyphrases.

views.name: paper_keyphrase_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paperId,
  keyphraseId
FROM paperKeyphrase

params.description: Which keyphrases are associated with each paper (paper–keyphrase link table).
params.when_to_use: List all keyphrases assigned to a given paper or all papers for a given keyphrase. | Filter or join papers by presence/absence of specific keyphrases. | Build counts or aggregates of keyphrases per paper when composed with an aggregation. | Compose with other paper-level views to add keyphrase membership as a filter or dimension.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from base table column paperKeyphrase.paperId | keyphraseId: identifier of the keyphrase linked to the paper — derived from base table column paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId
params.metric: No intrinsic numeric metrics in this view; all outputs are identifiers (no aggregates). If you need counts, derive them by aggregating this view, e.g. keyphrase_count_per_paper = COUNT(keyphraseId) GROUP BY paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base (or any other paper-level one-row-per-paper view such as paper_with_venue_journal, paper_citation_counts_agg if it is one-row-per-paper) on paperId — safe because paper_base is one-row-per-paper and this view is one-row-per (paperId, keyphraseId); joining will produce one row per keyphrase for that paper and will not duplicate measures from the one-row-per-paper side as long as those measures are interpreted at the paper–keyphrase grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_keyphrases (JOIN sibling) on (paperId, keyphraseId) — safe because it should represent the same linking grain; no duplication if both are the same granularity. | do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many child tables of paper (for example a paper_authors view that is one-row-per-author-per-paper) without re-aggregation, because joining paper_keyphrase (one-row-per paper–keyphrase) to a one-to-many authors-per-paper table will multiply rows and thus multiply any aggregated measures derived from either side. To combine counts from both dimensions safely, first aggregate to a common grain (e.g., aggregate paper_keyphrase to counts per paper or aggregate authors to counts per paper) and then join at the paperId grain. | do NOT join to many-to-many or multiple one-to-many tables simultaneously at their detailed grains without planning for multiplicative effects. If you need cross-dimension aggregates (e.g., number of keyphrases and number of authors per paper), compute each metric separately at the paper grain and then join those aggregated results on paperId. | If you need a per-keyphrase metric, you can aggregate this view by keyphraseId (e.g., papers_per_keyphrase = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY keyphraseId) and then join to keyphrase-dimension tables (if present) on keyphraseId — safe because the aggregation removes the paper-level multiplicity prior to the join.

views.description: Which keyphrases are associated with each paper (paper–keyphrase link table).

views.name: keyphrase_paper_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  k.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pk.paperId) AS paper_count
FROM keyphrase k
LEFT JOIN paperKeyphrase pk ON pk.keyphraseId = k.keyphraseId
GROUP BY k.keyphraseId

params.description: For each keyphrase (keyphraseId), counts the number of distinct papers associated with that keyphrase.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of papers tagged with a specific keyphrase or a set of keyphrases (single-keyphrase or multi-keyphrase filters after join). | Seed for ranking keyphrases by popularity (paper count) or for categorical aggregation by keyphrase. | Compose with keyphrase metadata (e.g., keyphrase text or category) to produce reports or dashboards showing paper counts per keyphrase. | Join as a pre-aggregated measure when computing ratios or rates that require paper counts per keyphrase combined with other per-keyphrase metrics.
params.output_schema: keyphraseId: identifier for the keyphrase; derived from base table column keyphrase.keyphraseId. | paper_count: number of distinct papers associated with that keyphrase; derived from COUNT(DISTINCT paperKeyphrase.paperId) in the aggregation.
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperKeyphrase.paperId) grouped by keyphrase.keyphraseId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to the keyphrase (dimension) view/table on keyphraseId — e.g., join keyphrase_paper_counts.keyphraseId = keyphrase.keyphraseId — safe because keyphrase_paper_counts is one-row-per-keyphrase, so its paper_count measure will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any other one-row-per-keyphrase aggregate or normalized keyphrase view (if present) on keyphraseId; these one-to-one joins do not change the meaning of paper_count. | do NOT directly join keyphrase_paper_counts to paperKeyphrase or to any other one-to-many table/view keyed by keyphraseId (for example, a raw paperKeyphrase join or a join to paper_authors filtered by paper) without re-aggregation — joining a one-row-per-keyphrase aggregated view to a child one-to-many relation will multiply the rows and therefore duplicate paper_count unless you re-aggregate after the join. | if you need to combine paper_count with other measures from one-to-many relations (e.g., counts of datasets per keyphrase obtained by joining through papers), join keyphrase_paper_counts to the dimension you need (keyphrase) and compute additional aggregates from the one-to-many side independently, then join the resulting per-keyphrase aggregates. views.name: paper_with_authors
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.title,
  p.year,
  p.numCiting,
  a.authorId,
  a.authorName
FROM paper AS p
JOIN writes AS w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
JOIN author AS a ON w.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: A per-paper-per-author flattened view listing paper metadata together with each of its authors (one row per paperId + authorId).
params.when_to_use: List all authors for a given paper (by paperId, title, or year). | List all papers authored by a specific author (by authorId or authorName). | Compose author-level aggregations from per-paper rows when you want to preserve one row per paper-author before aggregating. | Join paper metadata to author attributes while preserving paper-level measures (e.g., numCiting) at the paper-author granularity. | Use as the driving table for queries that need both paper and author dimensions without aggregating across authors.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived from table paper.paperId (base column in FROM). | title: paper title string — derived from table paper.title. | year: publication year of the paper — derived from table paper.year. | numCiting: number of times the paper is cited — derived from table paper.numCiting (treated as a paper-level metric/measure). | authorId: unique identifier of the author for this paper — derived from table author.authorId via writes.authorId join. | authorName: display name of the author — derived from table author.authorName.
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.year | paper.numCiting | writes.paperId | writes.authorId | author.authorId | author.authorName
params.metric: numCiting = paper.numCiting  -- a paper-level measure taken directly from the paper table (no aggregation in this view).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base on paperId — safe because paper_base is normalized to one row per paper (one-row-per-paperId), so joining on paperId will not duplicate this view's rows or multiply paper-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity on authorId — safe because author_identity is normalized to one row per author (one-row-per-authorId), so joining on authorId will not duplicate rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe if paper_with_venue_journal is one-row-per-paper (it is a JOIN that preserves paper grain); confirm it is one-row-per-paper before relying on no-duplication. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many children of paper (e.g., paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, citation_edges representing many incoming/outgoing edges, paper_authorship if it expands authorship further) without re-aggregating or deduplicating first — those joins will multiply rows per paperId (and therefore multiply paper-level measures such as numCiting) because paper_with_authors already has one row per (paperId, authorId). | If you need to combine with paper-level aggregates (e.g., paper_citation_counts_agg, papers_per_venue_agg), join those aggregates on paperId or venueId respectively — safe because those are pre-aggregated to one row per aggregation key; ensure you join on the matching key (paperId for paper-level aggregates). | If you need to compute author-level aggregates from this view (e.g., count of papers per author, sum of numCiting per author), first GROUP BY authorId (and other desired author keys) to avoid double-counting when later joining to other one-to-many author children. | When composing with sibling JOIN views that are many-to-many relative to (paperId, authorId), use a strategy: (a) aggregate the many-side to the same grain as this view before joining, or (b) join on keys that preserve uniqueness (e.g., join to author_identity on authorId), or (c) perform joins in subqueries that deduplicate keys to prevent measure multiplication. | Examples of unsafe direct joins (will multiply rows/measures): join to paper_keyphrases on paperId without aggregation, join to citation_edges to enumerate citing edges without first aggregating counts, join to paper_datasets when a paper can have multiple datasets. Instead, join to their corresponding *_agg views (paper_citation_counts_agg, papers_per_venue_agg, papers_per_author_agg) when you need summarized info.

views.name: papers_with_authors_denorm
views.body_sql:

  w.paperId AS paperId,
  p.title AS title,
  p.year AS year,
  w.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  p.journalId AS journalId
FROM writes w
JOIN paper p ON p.paperId = w.paperId
JOIN author a ON a.authorId = w.authorId

params.description: A denormalized row-per-authorship view that lists papers together with the author who wrote them and basic paper identifiers (venue, journal) — answers questions about individual paper-author relationships and enables counting or further aggregation per paper, author, venue, or journal.
params.when_to_use: List all paper-author pairs with paper metadata (title, year, venueId, journalId). | Filter or search papers by author (or authors by paper) and return paper details. | Compose higher-level aggregates like counts of papers per author, papers per venue, or papers per year by aggregating this view. | Join to author-level or paper-level dimensions (one-to-one) to enrich rows with additional attributes. | Build downstream JOINs that require the grain of one row per (paperId, authorId).
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived from writes.paperId (base table writes) | title: paper title — derived from paper.title (base table paper) | year: publication year of the paper — derived from paper.year (base table paper) | authorId: unique identifier of the author for this authorship row — derived from writes.authorId (base table writes) | authorName: display name of the author for this authorship row — derived from author.authorName (base table author) | venueId: identifier of the venue associated with the paper (may be NULL) — derived from paper.venueId (base table paper) | journalId: identifier of the journal associated with the paper (may be NULL) — derived from paper.journalId (base table paper)
params.grounded_columns: writes.paperId | writes.authorId | paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.year | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | author.authorId | author.authorName
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) OVER ()  -- implicit measure: counts rows at the (paperId, authorId) grain if aggregated appropriately | There are no pre-computed aggregate metrics in this view. All columns are base attributes; aggregates (counts, distinct counts, etc.) must be computed by aggregating this view at the desired grain (for example: COUNT(*) GROUP BY authorId to get papers_per_author).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity (NORM) on authorId — safe because this view is at most one row per writes.authorId per writes.paperId and author_identity is one-row-per-authorId; joining will not duplicate measures from this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_base or paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe because those are one-row-per-paperId dimensions and will not duplicate this view's rows. | cardinality-UNSAFE warning: do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child of paper (for example paper_datasets, paper_keyphrases, citation_edges if modeled as many edges per paper, or paper_authorship if that is another multi-row authorship representation) without first aggregating or deduplicating. Because this view already has one row per (paperId, authorId), joining to another table that has multiple rows per paperId (or per (paperId, authorId)) will multiply rows and therefore multiply any counts/metrics derived from this view. | composition recommendation: to combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., paper_datasets or paper_keyphrases), either (a) aggregate the child to the same grain as this view (paperId or (paperId, authorId) as appropriate) before joining, or (b) aggregate this view after the join to the intended analytic grain to avoid double-counting. | example safe compositions: aggregate this view to author-level (GROUP BY authorId) then join to papers_per_author_agg or author_paper_counts_ranked for comparisons; or aggregate to paper-level (GROUP BY paperId) before joining to paper_citation_counts_agg. | note on joins to sibling JOIN views: confirm sibling view grain.
